\subsection{Internal row reserve and ordinary conversion}
The finite cover requires a row divisor $W(w)$ at each coarse level.
All children have ratio at most $66/67$ and depth
$D(n)\le47\lceil\log_2\max(2,n)\rceil+O(1)$.
A sufficient common divisor is $W(w)^{D(n)}$ times the inherited old-leaf
reserve. The old supplier has its retained complete-row contract and
logarithmic reserve. Therefore a sufficient integer $S(e,w)$ satisfies
\[
 \log_qS(e,w)=O(w\log e).
\]
Unused stock is divided only into fresh descendant role fields; exposed
parent low/high fields are spectator prefixes. Their weights cannot depend
on those fresh roles. Every completed call restores its row coordinate,
so successive residuals and the outer wrapper reuse one reserve instead
of multiplying reserves for sequential calls.

The unweighted reversed endpoint $F_n(H,D)=(C_nD,C_nH)$ converts to an
ordinary interchange by the chronological sequence
\[
 D\leftarrow D-H;\quad F_n;\quad D\leftarrow D+H;\quad
 F_n;\quad D\leftarrow H-D.
\]
Indeed the successive values are $(H,D-H)$, $(C_n(D-H),C_nH)$,
$(C_n(D-H),C_nD)$, $(D,D-H)$, and $(D,H)$.
The three additive maps cost $O(Vn)$ in the atom model. The two calls
reuse restored rows; their constant multiplicity is outside the recursion
and does not multiply its characteristic moment.

\subsection{Borrowing and restoring the stock}
Set $\beta=1/1000$, $w=\lceil e^\beta\rceil$, and
$k=\lceil\log_qS(e,w)\rceil=O(w\log e)$, using the depth bound for the
original width $e$. For sufficiently large $e$, $k<e/2$. Write the two
original complete radix-$q$ chunks as $H=(H_{\rm hi},H_{\rm body})$ and
$D=(D_{\rm hi},D_{\rm body})$, both high parts having $k$ digits. The
physical order, including arbitrary original complete spectators $Z$, is
\[
 H_{\rm hi},\ H_{\rm body},\ Z,\ D_{\rm hi},\ D_{\rm body}.
\]
The complete $q^k$ range of $H_{\rm hi}$ already precedes both bodies.
Reinterpret it as a preceding row field; $D_{\rm hi}$ remains an intervening
spectator. Pad only this row range to $\lceil q^k/S\rceil S$. As $q^k\ge S$,
the padding factor is less than two.

Execute the completed \emph{ordinary} body wrapper with this row reserve,
then remove the padding. Each row is restored, so the genuine row range
is invariant at the completed endpoint. The order of values is now
\[
 H_{\rm hi},\ D_{\rm body},\ Z,\ D_{\rm hi},\ H_{\rm body}.
\]
One inherited ordinary width-$k$ interchange of the two high parts,
with the bodies and $Z$ as spectators, gives
\[
 D_{\rm hi},\ D_{\rm body},\ Z,\ H_{\rm hi},\ H_{\rm body}.
\]
This is precisely the original full-chunk interchange. Its extra cost is
$O(Vk^{1-a_{\rm old}})\le O(Vw\log e)$, conservatively. No full body is
moved once per borrowed digit. Padding occurs only in this outer wrapper;
it contributes one volume constant, not a recursive branching factor.
The wrapper does not rely on a raw reversed call preserving borrowed high
positions. Small widths use the retained supplier directly.

\subsection{Uniform saving and return to binary addresses}
Select atom width from the original $e$. Since $k=o(e)$, the body width
$e-k$ has the same asymptotic powers as $e$. Apply the ordinary wrapper to
its complete atom body and the old ordinary supplier to fewer than $w$
remaining digits. The stopped recurrence and the borrowing cost give
\[
 O\!\left(V\left[e^{1-\beta}+
 e^{(1-\beta)(1-a)+\beta(1-a_{\rm old})}+e^\beta\log e\right]\right).
\]
Here $a=747/2000000$ and $a_{\rm old}=384599/10^{10}$. Set
\[
 a_{\rm bit}=(1-\beta)a+\beta a_{\rm old}
 =\frac{3731649599}{10^{13}}=0.0003731649599.
\]
The inequalities $\beta>a_{\rm bit}$ and $\beta<1-a_{\rm bit}$ make both
the atom-adapter and borrowing terms lower order. The remainder cost
$O(Vw^{1-a_{\rm old}})$ is also covered. Thus the ordinary radix-$q$
interchange has cost $O(Ve^{1-a_{\rm bit}})$, without an externally supplied
superpolynomial stock of rows.

For an original binary chunk range $[2^e]$, let
$t=\lceil e/\log_2q\rceil$ and embed it numerically into $[q^t]$.
Pad both exchanged ranges while retaining every spectator. The total
logical-volume increase is below $q^2$. Execute the completed ordinary
radix-$q$ interchange, then remove the padding. Its endpoint preserves the
rectangular genuine set $[2^e]\times[2^e]$; intermediate maps may mix genuine
and padded addresses, which does not affect this endpoint justification.
As $q$ is fixed and $t=\Theta(e)$, the binary interchange has the same
saving exponent. All schedules use a fixed number of finite-alphabet
tapes; low residue tables and port types are fixed independently of $w$.

The conclusion retains the original local-producer, ordered-affine,
ordinary-leaf and multiplication-framework hypotheses. It adds no free
unit-scaling, dense chart transformation, or external row-stock primitive.
